record.original_question: Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system and let u <= v in W. Must there always exist another Coxeter system (W',S') and an element w in W' such that the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) can be realized as P_{e,w}(q)?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.9. Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system and u,v in W, u <= v. Is it true that then there are a Coxeter system (W',S') and w in W' such that P_{u,v}(q) = P_{e,w}(q)?

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this specific question (whether every Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial $P_{u,v}$ in some Coxeter system can be realized as $P_{e,w}$ in some possibly different Coxeter system). General references on Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials and Bruhat-interval isomorphism results were found, but none that confirm or refute the realization problem in full generality. Status appears to remain unknown / open based on available evidence.
